definition: Extremely old or old-fashioned
example: His antediluvian phone still has a cord.

definition: Widely told but probably not true
example: That story about the president is apocryphal.

definition: Using long words to sound important
example: His bombastic speech bored the crowd.

definition: A loud and unpleasant mix of sounds
example: A cacophony of horns filled the street.

definition: The use of tricks to deceive
example: The lawyer accused him of financial chicanery.

definition: Aware of or knowing about something
example: She is cognizant of the risks involved.

definition: In good order or completely fine
example: After the talk, everything felt copacetic.

definition: A complete and shameful failure
example: The launch turned into a public debacle.

definition: To throw someone out of a window
example: The angry king had his rival defenestrated.

definition: The final part of a story where things are resolved
example: The novel's denouement surprised every reader.

definition: Done without plan or purpose
example: He made a desultory attempt at cleaning.

definition: Light and almost see-through
example: She wore a diaphanous silk scarf.

definition: A level or rank within an organization
example: He reached the top echelon of the firm.

definition: Full of energy and excitement
example: Her effervescent laugh fills every room.

definition: Very bad and easily noticed
example: The report contained egregious errors.

definition: Lasting for a very short time
example: Fame can be ephemeral — enjoyed briefly and quickly forgotten.

definition: To use ambiguous language to avoid commitment or to mislead
example: The politician equivocated rather than giving a direct answer.

definition: Showing great knowledge from long study
example: The erudite professor spoke five languages.

definition: Known or understood by only a few
example: His research covers esoteric parts of physics.

definition: Very concerned about small details
example: He is fastidious about his shoes staying clean.

definition: Talking a lot, often about small things
example: My garrulous uncle told the same story twice.

definition: Using fancy language to sound impressive
example: The mayor gave a grandiloquent farewell speech.

definition: Used so often it has lost meaning
example: The film relies on hackneyed jokes.

definition: A person who attacks common beliefs
example: The artist was an iconoclast of his time.

definition: Too great to describe in words
example: She felt an ineffable joy at her wedding.

definition: Impossible to understand or read
example: His inscrutable face gave nothing away.

definition: Likely to cry or make people cry
example: The lachrymose ending made me weep.

definition: Clear and easy to see through
example: The limpid lake reflected the sky.

definition: A situation of great confusion or trouble
example: The country fell into a maelstrom of protest.

definition: Sweet and smooth to hear
example: She has a mellifluous singing voice.

definition: The lowest point of something
example: That loss was the nadir of his career.

definition: To make something hard to understand
example: The report obfuscates the real numbers.

definition: Trying too hard to please someone in power
example: The obsequious waiter praised every dish.

definition: A solution said to fix all problems
example: Technology is not a panacea for schools.

definition: Very clear and easy to follow
example: The teacher gave a pellucid explanation.

definition: Done quickly with little care
example: He gave a perfunctory nod and left.

definition: Having a ready insight; showing great mental penetration or discernment
example: A perspicacious observer noticed the flaw in the argument immediately.

definition: Giving a good chance of success; favorable
example: The clear skies were propitious for the outdoor ceremony.

definition: Showing a lack of courage
example: His pusillanimous silence angered the crowd.

definition: Full of hope but unlikely to succeed
example: Her quixotic plan to end hunger inspired many.

definition: Refusing to obey or cooperate
example: The recalcitrant student ignored the teacher.

definition: Good for your health
example: The town has a salubrious mountain climate.

definition: Hopeful and positive about the future
example: She remains sanguine about the election.

definition: The philosophical idea that only one's own mind is certain to exist
example: His solipsism made it difficult for him to empathize with others.

definition: Making you feel sleepy
example: The long lecture had a soporific effect.

definition: Done in secret to avoid notice
example: He took a surreptitious photo of the painting.

definition: A person who flatters others excessively to gain advantage
example: Surrounded by sycophants, the leader never heard honest advice.

definition: Quick to argue or become violent
example: The truculent fan shouted at the referee.

definition: A change in circumstances, often unwelcome
example: He faced the vicissitudes of army life.

definition: A soft, gentle breeze
example: A cool zephyr moved through the trees.
